text:
Published HSTU text fusion supports addition, but the closest implementation found, HSTU-BLaIR, uses pretrained text embeddings: input fusion is e_ID + W_text e_text; sampled candidate embeddings are separately projected and L2-normalized. It does not establish an optimal fusion coefficient or a vocabulary/truncation/missing-text recipe for jointly trained, randomly initialized text encoders. These details require explicit experimental choices rather than attribution to that paper. [HSTU-BLaIR](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf)

A reproducible proposed adaptation: train token embeddings jointly with HSTU, masked-mean pool title/description tokens, project to ID dimension, and fuse as e_ID + α·t. Compare unscaled addition against branch normalization with a learned scalar gate; report branch norms and α. Build vocabulary from training-item metadata, specifying tokenizer, frequency threshold, size cap and deterministic ordering; reserve PAD/UNK. Torchtext implements frequency thresholds, vocabulary caps and OOV mapping. Specify title/description token budgets and truncation direction; force missing-text contribution to zero even after biased projections, and preserve padding zeros. These are proposed controls, not validated HSTU defaults. [Vocabulary implementation](https://docs.pytorch.org/text/stable/vocab.html)

Proposed ablations: ordinary ID-only HSTU; parameter-matched ID-only HSTU with an active residual MLP; identical text architecture retrained after a fixed item-to-text permutation. Shuffle complete texts within category, preserving missingness, then additionally within training-popularity and text-length bins. Strip brand/model identifiers from available text and repeat aligned-versus-shuffled comparisons. Preserve architecture, training budget, seeds, splits and scoring normalization. Improvements over these controls support useful alignment but do not prove semantic transfer; inspect head/tail results alongside macro validation HR@10. Train each ablation separately; retain one checkpoint per category and never fuse predictions.
